operations_plan.summary: Extract the existing clevis-bore axis, bore diameter, and outside lug span to define a coaxial pivot pin without changing the lever body.

steps.description: Inspect the two cylindrical bearing surfaces assigned to the coaxial clevis pin bore. Confirm that faces 0 and 1 are coaxial, have radius 3 mm, and share an axis parallel to Y. Create or retrieve a datum axis from their common cylindrical axis; this is the required rotation axis and pin centerline.

Retrieve the minimum and maximum Y coordinates of the exterior faces of the two clevis lugs, using the axial bounds of bore faces 0 and 1 and the surrounding paired lug geometry as references. Define two datum planes normal to Y at these outside boundaries. Their separation defines a pin length that spans both lugs and the intervening 7 mm clevis slot, with the pin ends flush to the outside lug faces. Do not use slot-wall faces 3 and 4 as the pin endpoints because they bound only the internal gap.

operations_plan.summary: Create a new, separate cylindrical pin through the aligned clevis bores, coaxial with the Y-directed pivot axis and sized for rotational clearance.

steps.description: Create a sketch on the negative-Y outside-lug datum plane established in operation_01_step_02. Project the datum axis from operation_01_step_01 onto the sketch and place a concentric circle at that point. Define the pin radius as 3 mm minus a positive radial clearance, or equivalently define its diameter as 6 mm minus the selected diametral clearance. The clearance value is unresolved because the request does not specify a fit or manufacturing standard; use the project-standard running or sliding clearance fit. If no clearance standard is available, retain 6 mm as the nominal pin diameter but keep the pin as a separate body.

Extrude the circular profile along positive Y, coaxial with the datum axis, using an up-to-plane extent to the positive-Y outside-lug datum plane. Create the extrusion as a new solid rather than adding or fusing it to solid 0. The resulting new section is the pivot pin and must pass continuously through the negative-Y lug bore, the central clevis slot, and the positive-Y lug bore.

Preserve the cylindrical pin as an independent solid or component and assign a concentric revolute relationship between its cylindrical axis and the common axis of bore faces 0 and 1. Do not apply a rigid union, press-fit constraint, or axial retention feature because the request does not specify whether the pin or lever is stationary or how the pin is retained. The intended kinematic result is one rotational degree of freedom about Y, with axial translation suppressed only if an assembly constraint is required.

Validate that the new pin is coaxial with both bore segments, spans the full outside-to-outside clevis width, and does not interfere with the preserved bearing surfaces when the selected clearance is applied. Confirm that solid 0 is unchanged: retain the radius-3 mm bore faces 0 and 1, slot walls 3 and 4, rounded lug surfaces 6 and 15, the complete tapered spine, and the opposite hook section. Do not add chamfers, heads, grooves, clips, or other retention geometry unless separately specified.
